examples.en: The lion's mane is blowing in the wind.

examples.ko: 말의 갈기를 빗으로 곱게 빗어 줬어요.
examples.en: I combed the horse's mane neatly with a comb.
A male lion can be told apart from a female by its mane.

examples.ko: 이 말은 갈기 색이 특히 예뻐요.
examples.en: This horse has an especially pretty mane color.

examples.ko: 갈기에 먼지가 잔뜩 붙어서 털어 주었어요.
examples.en: Dust was stuck all over its mane, so I brushed it off.
I saw a horse at the zoo whose mane was golden too.

explain: 사자나 말의 목덜미에 길게 자란 털을 말하고, 말에게는 '말갈기'라고도 해요. '갈기갈기 찢다', '갈기다'와 소리가 비슷하지만 서로 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: The horse's mane felt soft when I stroked it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말의 갈기만 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers specifically to a horse's mane.

phrases.en: That male lion has a long, handsome mane.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사와 함께 모습을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with adjectives to describe appearance.

phrases.en: The horse runs with its mane flying.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달리는 동물의 멋진 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a vivid picture of a running animal.

explain_en: It is the long hair on the neck of a lion or horse, and for horses it is also called '말갈기'. It sounds similar to '갈기갈기 찢다' (tear to pieces) and '갈기다', but they are different words.

examples.ko: 이 길은 오른쪽으로 조금 경사져 있어요.
examples.en: This road slopes a little to the right.
The floor is slanted, so the ball keeps rolling.
I was out of breath climbing the sloped hill road.

examples.ko: 지붕이 경사지면 눈이 잘 미끄러져 내려와요.
examples.en: If the roof is sloped, snow slides down easily.
It's an old house, so the floor tilts to one side.

examples.ko: 경사지게 만든 주차장이라 브레이크를 꼭 밟아야 해요.
examples.en: The parking lot is built on a slope, so you must press the brake.

explain: '경사진 길'처럼 뒤에서 꾸며 주는 모양으로 가장 많이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '비스듬하다'나 '기울어 있다'도 자주 말해요. 반대는 '평평하다'예요.

phrases.en: Ride your bike slowly on a sloped road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 가장 흔한 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form, placed before a noun.

phrases.en: The floor isn't sloped, so water collects.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기울지 않고 평평하다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it doesn't tilt and is flat.

phrases.en: The desk is tilted to one side.
phrases.nuance_ko: '경사지다'보다 일상 대화에서 더 쉽고 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more common in daily talk than '경사지다'.

explain_en: It is most often used before a noun, as in '경사진 길'. In everyday speech people also say '비스듬하다' or '기울어 있다'. The opposite is '평평하다' (flat).

examples.en: The autumn sky is really high and blue.
We ate lunch boxes under the high blue sky.
After the rain stopped, the sky cleared up high and blue.
The high blue sky was soon dyed with the sunset.
On a clear, high blue day, I want to go for a walk.
I was amazed because the sky in the photo was so high and blue.

explain: 주로 맑은 가을 하늘을 묘사할 때 써요. 글이나 노래에서 많이 나오고, 말할 때는 "하늘이 높고 파래요"라고도 해요. '푸르다'처럼 '러' 불규칙이라 '높푸르러요'로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: Looking at the high blue sky made me feel good.
phrases.nuance_ko: '높푸른'으로 하늘을 꾸미는 가장 흔한 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use, describing the sky with '높푸른'.

phrases.en: Yesterday the rain stopped and the sky was high and blue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형이에요. '러' 불규칙이라 '높푸르렀어요'로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form. It is a '러' irregular, so it becomes '높푸르렀어요'.
phrases.en_equiv: the sky was high and blue

phrases.example: 하늘이 높푸르러서 소풍 가기에 딱 좋아요.
phrases.en: The sky is high and blue, so it's perfect for a picnic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 나타내는 연결형이에요. '높푸르러서'로 바뀌는 것도 '러' 불규칙이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form giving a reason, also changing to '높푸르러서' as a '러' irregular.

explain_en: It is mostly used to describe a clear autumn sky. It appears often in writing and songs, and in speech people may also say '하늘이 높고 파래요'. Like '푸르다' it is a '러' irregular verb, so it becomes '높푸르러요'.

examples.ko: 오리는 발에 물갈퀴가 있어서 헤엄을 잘 쳐요.
examples.en: Ducks have webbed feet, so they swim well.

examples.ko: 수영할 때 물갈퀴처럼 생긴 장갑을 꼈어요.
examples.en: I wore gloves shaped like webbed hands when I swam.

examples.ko: 물갈퀴만 있으면 사람도 오리처럼 빨리 헤엄칠까요?
examples.en: If people had webbed feet, could we swim as fast as ducks?

examples.ko: 물갈퀴는 헤엄칠 때 물을 힘껏 밀어 줘요.
examples.en: Webbed feet push the water hard when swimming.

examples.ko: 백조 발에서도 물갈퀴를 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see webbing on a swan's feet too.

examples.ko: 오리는 물갈퀴로 물을 밀면서 앞으로 나가요.
examples.en: Ducks move forward by pushing the water with their webbed feet.

explain: 오리, 개구리 같은 동물의 발가락 사이에 있는 얇은 막이에요. 사람이 수영할 때 신는 '오리발'도 모양이 비슷해서 가끔 물갈퀴라고 부르기도 해요. 보통은 동물 이야기에서 가장 많이 만나요.

phrases.example: 오리는 물갈퀴 달린 발로 걸어 다녀요.
phrases.en: Ducks walk around on webbed feet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물의 발 모양을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the shape of an animal's feet.

phrases.en: Frogs swim with their webbed feet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물갈퀴의 역할을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe what webbed feet are for.

phrases.en: I swam in the sea wearing fins.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 수영할 때 신는 물갈퀴 모양의 도구를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The fin-shaped gear that people wear when swimming.

explain_en: It is the thin skin between the toes of animals like ducks and frogs. Swim fins, called '오리발', look similar, so people sometimes call them '물갈퀴' too. You will meet it mostly when talking about animals.

examples.en: I watched a seal show at the aquarium.
The seal balances a ball on its nose.
Seals catch and eat fish in the sea.

examples.ko: 아이들이 귀여운 물개 앞에서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: The children took photos in front of the cute seal.

examples.ko: 저는 물개를 실제로 본 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I have never seen a seal in real life.
There was a child clapping like a seal.

explain: 물개는 바다에 사는 동물이에요. 수족관에서 공을 받고 박수 치는 모습으로 가장 많이 알려져 있어요. 팔을 앞으로 내밀고 손뼉을 치는 모습을 '물개 박수'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: The children clapped excitedly like seals.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팔을 앞으로 내밀고 손뼉 치는 모습을 물개에 비유한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Compares clapping with arms stretched forward to a seal.

phrases.en: I saw seals at the zoo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물원이나 수족관에서 가장 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most common at a zoo or aquarium.

phrases.en: I gave my sibling a seal doll as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물개 모양의 인형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A doll shaped like a seal.

explain_en: A 물개 is a sea animal, best known from aquarium shows where it catches balls and 'claps'. People also say '물개 박수' for clapping with the arms held out in front.

examples.en: I caught loaches in the rice field.
Loaches are slippery and hard to catch by hand.
Chueotang is a soup made from loaches.
A loach swims along the bottom of the fish tank.
Children watched loaches at a country stream.

examples.ko: 비 온 뒤에 미꾸라지가 땅 위로 올라왔어요.
examples.en: After the rain, a loach came up onto the ground.

explain: 몸이 길고 미끄러운 민물고기로, 추어탕의 재료예요. '미꾸라지 한 마리가 온 웅덩이를 흐려 놓는다'는 속담처럼 나쁜 사람을 비유하기도 해요. '빠져나가는 사람'을 가리킬 때도 '미꾸라지 같다'고 해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 질문을 하면 미꾸라지처럼 빠져나가요.
phrases.en: slippery like a loach
phrases.nuance_ko: 곤란한 상황이나 책임에서 요리조리 빠져나가는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes someone who keeps slipping out of difficult situations or responsibility.

explain_en: A long, slippery freshwater fish used in chueotang. In the proverb 미꾸라지 한 마리가 온 웅덩이를 흐려 놓는다 it stands for one bad person. 미꾸라지 같다 also describes someone who slips out of trouble.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 민물 생선 요리로 유명해요.
examples.en: This restaurant is famous for freshwater fish dishes.
Crucian carp live in fresh water.

examples.ko: 민물과 바닷물이 만나는 곳에는 물고기가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many fish where fresh water and sea water meet.

examples.ko: 주말에 민물 낚시를 하러 강에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the river for freshwater fishing on the weekend.
Fresh water has no salty taste.
Have you ever eaten freshwater eel?

explain: 반대말은 '바닷물'이나 '짠물'이에요. 강과 호수의 물을 말하고, '민물고기', '민물 낚시', '민물장어'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙어서 자주 나와요. 장어도 '민물장어'와 바다에 사는 '붕장어'로 나눠 불러요.

phrases.en: The crucian carp is a freshwater fish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강이나 호수에 사는 물고기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fish that live in rivers or lakes.

phrases.en: I went freshwater fishing with my father on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바다가 아닌 강이나 호수에서 하는 낚시예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fishing done in a river or lake instead of the sea.

phrases.en: Freshwater eel is a food that gives you energy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바다 장어'와 구별해서 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A name used to tell it apart from saltwater eel.

explain_en: Its opposites are '바닷물' and '짠물'. It means the water of rivers and lakes, and it often comes before other words, as in '민물고기', '민물 낚시', and '민물장어'. Even eels are split into the freshwater '민물장어' and the sea-dwelling '붕장어'.

examples.ko: 동굴 천장에 박쥐가 거꾸로 매달려 있어요.
examples.en: Bats hang upside down from the cave ceiling.
Bats fly around at night looking for food.
I saw a bat on the balcony last night.
The children bought a bat-shaped balloon.

examples.ko: 박쥐는 새가 아니라 젖을 먹이는 동물이에요.
examples.en: A bat is not a bird but a mammal.
I wore a bat costume at the Halloween party.

explain: 박쥐는 새처럼 날지만 새가 아니라 젖을 먹이는 동물이에요. '박쥐 같은 사람'처럼 말하면 이쪽저쪽 편을 들며 자기 이익만 챙기는 사람이라는 안 좋은 뜻이 돼요. 이솝 우화에서 온 비유라서 한국에서도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: a person who switches sides
phrases.nuance_ko: 이쪽에도 저쪽에도 붙어서 자기에게 이로운 쪽만 따르는 사람을 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize someone who sides with whoever benefits them, switching between camps.

explain_en: A bat flies like a bird but is a mammal. Calling someone 박쥐 같은 사람 means a person who takes both sides to protect their own interest, which is a negative remark. The image comes from an Aesop fable and is widely used in Korean.

examples.en: The bird is pecking the tree with its beak.
An eagle's beak is very sharp.

examples.ko: 아기 새가 노란 부리를 크게 벌렸어요.
examples.en: The baby bird opened its yellow beak wide.
Ducks have flat bills.
Parrots have curved beaks.
The magpie flew off with a twig in its beak.

explain: 새의 입 부분이에요. 사람에게는 '입', 동물에게는 '주둥이'를 쓰는데, 새만은 '부리'라고 해요. 사람 입을 낮춰서 '주둥이'라고 하면 실례가 돼요.

phrases.en: The color of the bird's beak is very pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '의'를 붙여 어떤 새의 부리인지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the particle 의 to say whose beak it is.

phrases.example: 이 새는 부리가 뾰족해서 벌레를 잘 잡아요.
phrases.en: This bird has a pointed beak, so it catches bugs well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부리의 모양을 설명할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the shape of a beak.

phrases.en: A sparrow pecks at the bread with its beak.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새가 부리로 하는 행동을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing to describe what birds do with their beaks.

explain_en: A bird's mouth part. Humans have '입' and many animals '주둥이', but birds alone have '부리'. Calling a person's mouth '주둥이' is rude.

en: inside the mountains; heart of the mountains

examples.ko: 스님은 산중 작은 절에서 살고 계세요.
examples.en: The monk lives in a small temple deep in the mountains.

examples.ko: 산중이라서 밤에는 별이 아주 잘 보여요.
examples.en: It's deep in the mountains, so you can see stars very well at night.

examples.ko: 산중에 있는 식당까지 걸어서 한 시간 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes an hour on foot to reach the restaurant in the mountains.
I got lost deep in the mountains.
The morning air in the mountains is really clear.

examples.ko: 그는 산중으로 들어가 몇 년 동안 혼자 살았어요.
examples.en: He went into the mountains and lived alone for several years.

explain: 산중은 '산속'과 비슷하지만 더 깊고 외진 곳이라는 느낌이 있어요. 말할 때는 '산속'이 더 자연스럽고 산중은 글이나 이야기, 절·스님 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 보통 '깊은 산중'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: There is a small temple deep in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산중은 보통 '깊은'과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 산중 is usually paired with '깊은'.

phrases.en: I got lost in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 비슷하고, 말할 때는 '산속'이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning; '산속' sounds more natural in speech.

phrases.en: The monk lived in the mountains for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산에서 조용히 사는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a quiet life lived in the mountains.

explain_en: 산중 is close to '산속' but feels deeper and more remote. In speech '산속' is more natural; 산중 shows up in writing, stories and talk of temples and monks. It is usually used as '깊은 산중'.

examples.ko: 뒤꼍에 선 수양버들이 햇볕을 받아 눈부시게 아름다웠어요.
examples.en: The weeping willow standing in the backyard was dazzlingly beautiful in the sunlight.

examples.ko: 강가에 늘어선 수양버들 가지가 바람에 흔들려요.
examples.en: The branches of the weeping willows lining the riverside sway in the wind.
In spring, light green leaves sprout on the weeping willow.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 공원에 수양버들 한 그루가 있어요.
examples.en: There is one weeping willow in my neighborhood park.
I waited for my friend under the weeping willow.
A weeping willow's branches droop down.

explain: 버드나무 가운데 가지가 아래로 길게 늘어지는 나무를 말해요. 평소에는 그냥 '버드나무'라고도 부르고, 시나 노래, 그림에서 강가나 봄 풍경으로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The weeping willow branches sway gently in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무에서 길게 늘어진 가지를 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for the long drooping branches.

phrases.en: There are many willow trees by the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '수양버들'보다 '버드나무'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday talk, 버드나무 is more common than 수양버들.

phrases.en: Weeping willows hang down long beside the pond.
phrases.nuance_ko: '늘어지다'는 아래로 길게 처진 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 늘어지다 describes something hanging down in a long line.

explain_en: It is a kind of willow whose branches hang long and low. In everyday speech people may also just say '버드나무' (willow), and it often appears in poems, songs and paintings as part of a riverside or spring scene.

examples.ko: 비누는 알칼리 성질이 있어서 손이 건조해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Soap is alkaline, so your hands can get dry.

examples.ko: 알칼리성 세제는 기름때를 닦는 데 좋아요.
examples.en: Alkaline detergent is good for cleaning grease.

examples.ko: 이 건전지는 알칼리 건전지라서 오래 가요.
examples.en: This is an alkaline battery, so it lasts long.
If you mix an acid and an alkali, the properties change.

examples.ko: 알칼리가 센 청소용품은 장갑을 끼고 쓰세요.
examples.en: Wear gloves when you use a cleaning product with strong alkali.
I checked with litmus paper whether it was alkaline.

explain: 산성의 반대 성질을 말하고, 일상에서는 '알칼리성', '알칼리 건전지', '알칼리성 세제'처럼 자주 보여요. '산성, 중성, 알칼리성' 순서로 같이 외우면 편해요. 과학 수업에서는 '염기'라는 말도 쓰지만, 생활 속에서는 '알칼리'가 더 익숙해요.

phrases.en: This water is alkaline, so it tastes smooth.
phrases.nuance_ko: '산성'의 반대 성질을 말할 때 '성'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds '성' to name the property opposite to acidic.

phrases.en: I put alkaline batteries in the remote control.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생활에서 가장 자주 보는 짝말 중 하나예요.
phrases.nuance_en: One of the most common everyday pairings.

phrases.en: I cleaned the kitchen grease with an alkaline detergent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기름때를 닦는 청소용품을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for cleaning products that remove grease.

explain_en: It names the property opposite to acid, and in daily life it appears in '알칼리성', '알칼리 건전지' and '알칼리성 세제'. It helps to memorize it with '산성, 중성, 알칼리성'. Science class also uses the term '염기', but '알칼리' is more familiar in everyday life.

examples.ko: 산 북쪽은 응달져서 눈이 늦게 녹아요.
examples.en: The north side of the mountain is in shade, so the snow melts late.
Moss grows a lot in shady places.

examples.ko: 집 앞이 응달지면 겨울에 길이 얼기 쉬워요.
examples.en: If the front of your house is shady, the road freezes easily in winter.
This room is shaded by the building.

examples.ko: 응달지지 않은 쪽에 화분을 놓아 주세요.
examples.en: Please put the pot on the side that isn't shady.
It's a road between buildings, so it's always in shade.

explain: '응달진 곳'처럼 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 모양으로 자주 써요. '응달지다'는 '응달진, 응달져요, 응달졌어요'로 활용해요. 반대로 해가 잘 드는 곳은 '볕이 잘 들다'라고 말해요.

phrases.example: 응달진 골목에는 얼음이 아직 남아 있어요.
phrases.en: There is still ice left in the shady alley.
phrases.nuance_ko: '응달진'은 장소를 꾸미는 가장 흔한 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '응달진' is the most common form for modifying a place.

phrases.example: 뒷마당이 응달져서 꽃이 잘 안 자라요.
phrases.en: The backyard is shady, so flowers don't grow well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어서'를 붙여 그늘진 이유로 생기는 결과를 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-아/어서' you can state a result caused by the shade.

phrases.example: 이쪽 정원은 응달지지 않아서 채소가 잘 커요.
phrases.en: This side of the garden isn't shady, so vegetables grow well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 해가 잘 든다는 뜻을 간접적으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form indirectly says the spot gets good sun.

explain_en: It often appears before a noun, as in '응달진 곳' (a shady place). It conjugates as '응달진', '응달져요' and '응달졌어요'. For a place with plenty of sun, you say '볕이 잘 들다'.

en: to live independently; to lead an independent life

examples.ko: 이 꽃은 제주도 산에서 저절로 자생해요.
examples.en: This flower grows wild on its own in the mountains of Jeju.
We are surveying plants that grow naturally on the Korean Peninsula.

examples.ko: 이 나무는 우리나라에서 자생하지 않아서 수입했어요.
examples.en: This tree does not grow naturally in our country, so it was imported.

examples.ko: 산에서 자생한 버섯은 함부로 먹으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You should not eat mushrooms that grew wild in the mountains carelessly.
A pine tree was growing naturally in a crack of the rock.

examples.ko: 이 약초는 높은 산에서만 자생할 수 있어요.
examples.en: This medicinal herb can grow wild only on high mountains.

explain: 주로 식물에 쓰고, 사람이 심지 않았는데 저절로 자라는 모습을 가리켜요. '야생'과 가깝지만 야생은 동물에도 쓰고, 자생은 '그 지역에 원래 있는'이라는 느낌이 더 강해요. '자생식물', '자생지'처럼 합쳐서도 자주 써요. 사람이 주어일 때는 제 힘으로 살아간다는 뜻으로 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: There are many native plants on this mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 지역에 원래 자라는 식물을 가리키는 합친 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compound for plants that grow natively in a region.

phrases.en: This is the natural habitat of a rare flower.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물이 저절로 자라는 장소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The place where a plant grows naturally.

phrases.example: 씨앗을 안 뿌렸는데 꽃이 저절로 자랐어요.
phrases.en: I didn't sow seeds, but flowers grew on their own.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자생하다를 쉬운 말로 풀어 쓴 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to say 자생하다 in plain words.

explain_en: It is mainly used for plants growing on their own without anyone planting them. It is close to '야생' (wild), but '야생' also applies to animals, while '자생' stresses that the plant natively belongs to that area. It is often combined, as in '자생식물' and '자생지'. With a person as the subject it can mean living by one's own power.

examples.en: There are many garden trees in our yard.

examples.ko: 봄마다 정원수를 다듬는 일이 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Trimming the garden trees every spring is not easy.
My father planted a pine tree as a garden tree.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 정원수 몇 그루가 쓰러졌어요.
examples.en: A few garden trees fell down because of the typhoon.

examples.ko: 이 동네는 정원수 관리가 잘되어 있어요.
examples.en: The garden trees in this neighborhood are well maintained.

examples.ko: 정원수에 물을 주는 건 제가 맡았어요.
examples.en: I took charge of watering the garden trees.

explain: 집 마당이나 공원에 심어 가꾸는 나무를 말해요. 길가에 줄지어 심은 나무는 '가로수'라고 해서 서로 구별돼요. 일상에서는 그냥 '나무'라고도 하고, '정원수'는 나무를 관리하거나 심는 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I planted garden trees in the yard in spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무를 새로 심는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for planting new trees.

phrases.en: My father tends the garden trees every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무를 돌보고 관리하는 일에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for looking after and caring for trees.

phrases.en: The garden trees have grown so much that the house is shaded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간이 지나 나무가 커졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the trees have grown bigger over time.

explain_en: It refers to trees planted and cared for in a yard or park. Trees lined along a street are called '가로수', so the two are distinguished. In daily talk people often just say '나무', and '정원수' comes up mostly when talking about planting or caring for trees.

examples.ko: 그 새는 날개를 안 써서 날개가 퇴화했어요.
examples.en: That bird didn't use its wings, so its wings degenerated.
I heard cave fish have degenerated eyes.
If you don't use them for a long time, muscles degenerate too.
An organ that is degenerating is called a vestigial organ.

examples.ko: 외국어를 안 쓰면 실력이 퇴화할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you don't use a foreign language, your skills can decline.

examples.ko: 이 곤충은 날개가 퇴화한 채로 땅에서만 살아요.
examples.en: This insect lives only on the ground with its wings degenerated.

explain: '날개가 퇴화하다', '눈이 퇴화하다'처럼 몸의 기관이 주어일 때 가장 자연스러워요. 실력이나 능력이 떨어진다고 말할 때는 '떨어지다', '약해지다'가 더 일상적이에요.

phrases.en: The human body has degenerated organs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙는 형태로, 이미 작아진 기관을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun to point to an organ that has already shrunk.

phrases.en: If it isn't used, the organ gradually degenerates.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서서히 진행되는 변화를 말할 때 '점점'과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 점점 for a change that happens gradually.

phrases.example: 그 동물의 시력은 아직 퇴화하지 않았어요.
phrases.en: That animal's eyesight has not degenerated yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기능이 남아 있다고 말할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, for saying the function still remains.

explain_en: It sounds most natural with a body part as the subject, as in '날개가 퇴화하다' (wings degenerate). For skills or abilities getting worse, '떨어지다' or '약해지다' is more common in daily speech.
